scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Independent friendship-email reading assessment with original questions, pending pedagogical validation

questions.q: What makes Tomas decide that he should contact Robin?
choices: A teacher asks him to write a class report.
Visiting their changed old square reminds him how little they have talked.
Robin sends him a new football shirt.
The workshop plans to close permanently.
questions.explanation: The changed square makes Tomas think of Robin and their long silence.

choices: The old school has disappeared.
A new cinema has opened.
Every building has been painted red.
An empty shop has become a community workshop.
questions.explanation: The vacant shop is now a workshop with colourful paintings.

questions.q: What did Tomas learn from teaching two children to repair a light?
choices: You must have a professional qualification to help.
Only adults can teach children.
You can be useful while still learning yourself.
Carrying boxes is better than helping people directly.
questions.explanation: Tomas understands that beginners can contribute without already being experts.

questions.q: Why did Tomas initially choose simple tasks at the workshop?
choices: He felt nervous about meeting new people.
He had to stay outside the workshop.
The volunteers refused to let him help.
He was preparing for a mechanics exam.
questions.explanation: He made tea and carried boxes because he felt shy around strangers.

questions.q: What do old photographs add to the workshop?
choices: They prove the town has never changed.
They replace the need for people to meet.
They help neighbours share memories of the area's history.
They show only recently renovated buildings.
questions.explanation: Photos of the former fountain and cinema help people discuss the neighbourhood's past.

questions.q: Why does Tomas mention Robin's old photographs?
choices: He hopes Robin might share some at the open day.
He wants Robin to become a paid photographer.
He has lost all the workshop pictures.
He plans to sell them to a shop.
questions.explanation: He remembers Robin's pictures of everyday life and invites him to bring a few.

questions.q: What does Tomas mean by saying Robin need not prepare a speech?
choices: He wants Robin to stay silent during the event.
A short informal visit would be welcome.
Only volunteers are allowed to speak.
The event will not include any activities.
questions.explanation: The invitation makes clear that Robin need not perform or prepare.

questions.q: Why does Tomas offer a video call or a visit to Robin's town?
choices: He wants to avoid talking about the old square.
He does not want Robin to send photographs.
He needs Robin to help sell workshop tools.
He understands travelling to the open day may be difficult.
questions.explanation: The alternative options show respect for Robin's time and travel costs.

questions.q: What bothers Tomas about relying on social-media photos?
choices: They take too long to open.
They are usually taken in poor weather.
They cannot replace hearing Robin's real experiences.
They include too many pictures of school.
questions.explanation: Tomas wants to know about the new town directly rather than guessing from online images.

questions.q: What is the main message behind Tomas's final question?
choices: Their friendship should not depend on rare special events.
They should meet only on important holidays.
The workshop needs more photographers to continue.
Their former school should organise a reunion.
questions.explanation: He asks to reconnect in ordinary life rather than wait for a special occasion.
